messages:
Alex G: Quick question — we rolled out the analytics service and the pod is failing with 403 when trying to call S3. The pod uses a ServiceAccount created by Helm (analytics-chart). I checked our Terraform and we provisioned an aws_iam_role for irsa plus an aws_iam_role_policy_attachment, but the SA in k8s has no iam.amazonaws.com/role-arn annotation. Do we need to annotate the Helm SA or is there some RoleBinding step I missed? :thinking:

Maria L: You need the annotation on the actual k8s ServiceAccount. IRSA uses the SA annotation to map to the IAM role via the OIDC provider. RoleBinding/ClusterRoleBindings don't affect IRSA. If Helm creates the SA you can either: 1) set a value in the chart to add the annotation, or 2) patch the SA after deploy.

Samir K: Confirming Maria. Example SA YAML you want in analytics namespace:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: analytics-sa
  namespace: analytics
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/rdw-analytics-irsa-role
```
IRSA also requires the IAM role trust policy to allow the OIDC provider and the k8s subject like: `system:serviceaccount:analytics:analytics-sa`.

Alex G: Got it. Our terraform creates aws_iam_role and a `kubernetes_service_account` resource in a different repo, but the helm chart still creates the SA (duplicate). That explains the mismatch. What's the safest fix? Update Helm values to disable SA creation and let TF manage it? Or patch the helm SA with annotation?

Maria L: Safer to have a single source of truth. Either let k8s SA be managed by Terraform (disable SA in the chart) or have Helm manage it and add the annotation via Helm values. If you leave both creating SA you get a race and no annotation.

Priya R: Quick checklist: 
- Make sure namespace matches (analytics). `kubectl get sa analytics-sa -n analytics`
- Ensure IAM role trust policy includes the OIDC provider and subject `system:serviceaccount:analytics:analytics-sa`
- Confirm annotation key is `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` (not iam.amazonaws.com/role) — ours needs eks one on EKS.

Samir K: Minor terraform snippet if you want TF to manage the SA and annotate it:
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_service_account" "analytics_sa" {
  metadata {
    name      = "analytics-sa"
    namespace = kubernetes_namespace.analytics.metadata[0].name
    annotations = {
      "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = aws_iam_role.analytics_irsa.arn
    }
  }
}
```
And the aws_iam_role needs the assume_role_policy referencing the cluster OIDC issuer.

Alex G: Thanks. I'll open a quick PR to disable the SA in the Helm chart (set `serviceAccount.create=false`) and let TF own it. One quick question: any gotchas around rollout/order? If TF creates SA with annotation after Helm deploys the Deployment will pick it up automatically?

Maria L: Pods that were already running won't get the annotation retroactively; but annotation only matters at pod startup — the token controller uses projected tokens and the kubelet will request tokens for the SA. So restart the deployment (rolling restart) after SA exists with annotation. `kubectl rollout restart deployment/analytics -n analytics`

infra-bot: terraform plan completed: https://ci.internal/plan/rdw-analytics/6723 :white_check_mark:

Priya R: Also double-check serviceaccount name in the deployment spec matches the SA name exactly. Common slip: chart puts `serviceAccount.name: {{ .Release.Name }}` but TF named it `analytics-sa`.

Alex G: Awesome — will do that flow and ping when PR is up. Thanks all :+1:
